reviews.title: Terrible Support Team
reviews.text: I’m stranded without my keys and won’t be able to enter my home because of ‘policies and procedures’. Lost items should have tiers of priority. I didn’t report leaving my keys in the Waymo hours later; I reported it nearly immediately. And they’re keys, not a water bottle or a lipstick or some item I can go a few hours without. When asking the agent Rocel O for help, I was met with very clinical, cold responses. Agents should be able to help, I even offered to go to the depot myself to retrieve my keys myself but he refused to look into it any further or contact someone who’d be able to offer better assistance and information. It really is a no brainer. If I leave my keys and notice immediately, why is there no option of the Waymo coming back to me? And if there’s passengers, that’s fine, there should be an option to show up the depot yourself preemptively, whether the team has located the item yet or not, so that I may be able to retrieve it instantly if it’s an emergency. How am I supposed to go home? I have a puppy in my house and I was told ‘4 hours’. I feel beyond frustrated and near tears. What was supposed to be a quick errands turned into a nightmare. And Rocel O.’s rigid, unwilling to find a way to help further, demeanor was the worst support I’ve ever experienced in my life. I had to ask if he was a program or a person. Waymo is my preferred mode of transportation. It’s ALL I use to get around LA, and I’m a good customer. It’s an intuitive, hassle free, and peaceful

reviews.title: Drop off
reviews.text:
One Star – Unsafe Drop-Off and Poor Customer Service

I had a terrible experience with Waymo on October 31, 2026, in Orlando.

The vehicle turned onto a street before the entrance to my residential community and left us in a completely dark and unsafe location, during extremely heavy rain.

My companion and I had to walk home in the pouring rain and arrived completely soaked.

After reporting this serious safety concern, Waymo offered me only a $10 credit toward a future ride. I find this response extremely disappointing.

This was not simply an inconvenience. It was a passenger safety issue.

I expected a full refund, a proper investigation, and a more responsible response from Waymo.

One star. Very disappointing experience.

reviews.title: Completely Nightmare
reviews.text: This was the worse experience in my life to take a trip with this service ..a trip that supposed to take 12 min ended up on 46 min .. it took the most busy streets Brickell.. downtown ..the streets that you know you need to avoid if you want to be on time to any engagement...but not just that...the car never reached the drop off point, the droff point was in a facility in the middle of the highway...well the car left me on the other side where the only thing to do is cross the highway..I called the support and they said that they can't stop anywhere else ..I could not believe it ..that i was left out there ..a woman completely alone in the middle of the highway....this was a completely nightmare..the worse experience in my life and that no one was there to talk or try to explain or guide...it's like speaking with AI I will never go into one of these cars ...I prefer human interaction.

reviews.title: Wow. Not ready!
reviews.text:
I love tech and wanted this to be good - oh my this is not ready for prime time. A ride in vegas that according to google maps was 10 minutes (aria to venetian) took 25 minutes to start because of some obscene route, the pickup took 10 minutes because the van circled three (!) times to then stop in the middle of the road and finally when we got close to venetian instead of queueing in line it drove by and wanted to do another 20 minute loop and it then did not let us out of the car! Luckily when we were stopped in the middle of a extremly (6 lane!) intersection it opened the doors.

Scary to say the least! We called support the first time they were very nice but when it took the detour nobody picked up.

reading the reviews on here to me it feels as if the positive reviews seem to be farmed and the negative ones all look like this one :-)

reviews.title: Waymo believer…embarrassed to get in the new van
reviews.text: I’m a huge autonomous driving believer and have been a dedicated and early user of Waymo since it became available in San Francisco. With that caveat, I have to say that the new Waymo vans are horrible. The new value proposition is that I pay more to be uncomfortable and embarrassed, how did that pass rounds of checks? Just to list a few problems with the new vans: The doors take forever to open and close and they open two at a time, making the passenger feel exposed and uncomfortable the whole time. The suspension is terrible and the seats are uncomfortable. These “wagons” are ugly, which makes a difference when I’m paying a premium for what used to feel like a luxury experience. The vans take up way more of the road than the SUVs when they stop, or at least appear to do so, making pedestrians and drivers annoyed…and the only available target is me, the person sitting for five minutes in a stalled vehicle that’s taking up an entire lane of traffic with the entire side of the car open to all of the glares while to doors slooowly close.

reviews.title: Scary…
reviews.text: Now upon three occasions, I’ve had terrifying experiences in Waymo with little to no help… well actually no help. My first ride, It got us stuck in an alleyway for about 30 minutes, and the second ride it almost ran us into a fire truck that was coming near us and it even pulled closer to it as it was coming towards us. It gets worse… On my third ride I ended up getting out after it was doing circles over and over and then tried to drop us off in a very sketchy alleyway (as a woman) with men in the dark approaching and watching. We called support because we felt unsafe and while we were talking to them, their response was this is where we had to get out and there’s nothing else they could do. Their not able to control the car and I’m certainly not controlling the car… so who’s actually controlling the vehicle you might ask, well I guess I won’t find out because I won’t be riding again.

reviews.title: just book an uber
reviews.text: was a fan of waymo for a while - more affordable rides, similar arrival times. the past few weeks the ride times and pickup spots have become absolutely unacceptable. the pickups have been updating as the ride is arriving to be 1 MILE AWAY. not sure how i’m supposed to walk 20+ mins to go to the new pickup spot within 6 mins before the waymo leaves?? and the driving routes lately have been ridiculous. i’ll look at maps GPS and it’ll say it’s a 20 min drive (no freeway) and the waymo route will say it takes 1 HOUR 15 MINS with the 20 minute walk to get to the pickup. this journey with uber would take 20 mins but with waymo it’ll take an hour and a half for the same price! i reached out to customer service who provided zero information and ended with chat without helping me. i have cancelled my account and will be using uber from now on - it’s around the same cost and will take a direct route instead of adding over an hour to your drive for no reason ☺️

reviews.title: Cars gone wild
reviews.text:
Update: I have had two serious allergic reactions and another experience of a waymo vehicle taking the longest route possible.

I am disabled and the cars frequently don’t actually drop you off at your location nor around the corner. 

I have been dropped off more than two blocks away. 
I have really severe chronic pain and I am under weight. 
So, I had to rush to get to my appointment and I am not supposed to be burning calories.

Right now the weirdest experience happened which was that customer support called itself interrupting a call I was having with a doctor’s office. 
They claimed that they had gotten a concerned call that someone under 18 was driving the car. 

I am in the back seat and 45. 

I love the concept of Waymo. It’s why I gave it 3 stars when after 2 terrifying experiences and one that was just a number of confusing detours out of 7 rides. 

I like not stepping into a car that smells of old cigarettes or an entire bottle of cologne. I appreciate not having to listen to someone else’s music or talk to them if I am tired or not feel rude making an important call, but it’s a safety concern as well as a time concern when the car just starts driving somewhere else.

reviews.title: Keeps rescheduling rides
reviews.text: I’m late or to early to school to often, wait times are not accurate and rides are ALMOST ALWAYS RESCHEDULED it’s so annoying.  You will get a wait times saying 10 mins and then you check 5 mins later to see you’ve been rescheduled to 25 mins Beacuse it’s dropping off another rider. Also the car cuts people off in traffic a lot, if a lane isn’t moving fast enough it just swerves infront of somone if there’s room. It also waits to get into the Turing lane till the last second, if it needs to change lanes it just stops and stays still till somone lets it over, it holds up traffic so often and does the same during rush hour.

reviews.title: Not ready
reviews.text:
Cars will randomly decide to drive in the same circle repeatedly on pickup and drop off. Also, they never pick up or drop off in quite the right spot, even when they don't get stuck. Not ready for prime time at all.

What's more insulting is, when you contact support, they offer a $10 credit. Except the credit only applies to future rides and expires in 60 days.

Seriously? If you can't even stand behind your own product, why do you expect anyone else to trust it. If you're going to waste a rider's time and make them call support just to get the car unstuck — after which you still have the car try to pick up / drop off in the middle of a busy street rather than the safe parking lot selected — the least you could do is just offer an immediate credit off the cost of the ride. Frankly, the two rides I just took should have just been free, since the mess-ups nearly doubled the driving time.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with Waymo and their so-called “innovation.” While they market themselves as the future of transportation, what they’re really doing is taking away jobs from hardworking taxi and rideshare drivers who rely on that income to support their families. Not everyone has the luxury of transitioning into tech — some people depend on driving jobs to survive.
This push for fully autonomous taxis feels less like progress and more like corporate greed disguised as advancement. Instead of investing in communities and creating opportunities, they’re replacing people with machines. It’s frustrating to see technology prioritized over livelihoods.
The service itself may be high-tech, but at what social cost? Companies should be thinking about the real-world impact of their decisions, not just profits and headlines.
Very disappointed with the direction this is going

reviews.title: Left us stranded with 2 small children
reviews.text: We were kicked out of the car due to not having child seats to put the kids in. Are they serious? Were we supposed to carry car seats around with us? After we were driving for a few minutes a Waymo representative came on through the speakers. He proceeded to tell us how we were breaking the rules and violating their terms of use 3 different times like we were either children or dumb. I said “ok we get it” when he started to tell us the 4th  time. then he forced Waymo car to just pull over ini the middle of some random road. the Car did well, management did not. We had to walk another mile to get a taxi with a 3 year old…and a6year old. I’ll say it again….. A 3yo and a 6yo.

reviews.title: Not ready for prime time
reviews.text:
It’s neat but costs about the same as Uber/Lyft. We took a ride to the airport which should have taken about 15 minutes. This particular Waymo wouldn’t use the freeways and went local the entire way, taking 45 minutes. We reached out to support and this is their reply - “I apologize if the car took a long route. Unfortunately, our routes for freeway was still on roll out. This means that  there are limited trips that can go on a freeway.”   Not helpful and almost caused us to miss our flight. 

Additionally, the car would stay in the slow lane following a transit bus for miles then randomly switch lanes for no reason. Felt a bit confused. 

My seat belt constantly tightened and would not loosen at all. Uncomfortable all the way around.

reviews.title: Do Not Use Waymo
reviews.text: Where can I begin. I started using Waymo after my truck broke down and I was in between vehicles. The most common issue I faced was the late arrival of my ride. It had happened a couple of times during some weekends but I didn’t mind because I wasn’t in a hurry; however, between the first week of September - my rides were considerably late (often by 15-20 minutes) even when scheduling them. It became a major issue when I was consistently late to work that week by about 20 minutes on average. After reporting it the first time, I almost felt as though they were punishing me for reporting the issue as it kept reoccurring after exhausting the “solutions” provided by their support team. I also encountered several rides in which the vehicle would loop in a circle for no apparent reason. If you need a ride service, I would never recommend Waymo - you are far better off using Uber or Lyft.

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text: I have been using Waymo for over two years as a trusted tester and up until now everything had been fine and fair. I’ve had two really negative experiences with them. Don’t trust their pre-scheduling feature because it doesn’t work. They don’t reserve any specific ride for you so do expect to wait an additional 25 minutes to you’re already 30 minute wait additionally they’ll charge you $100 cleaning fee without providing any details on what ride it was supposed to be for and don’t expect to receive a refund right away when it’s there mistake because apparently it takes about 48 hours to investigate when they should’ve done the investigation before pulling the money out out of your bank account.
